This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Muffet

![demo](img/demo.gif)

Muffet is a fast website link checker which scrapes and inspects all pages in a website recursively.

## Features

- Massive speed
- High compatibility with web browsers
- Different tag support (`a`, `img`, `link`, `script`, etc)
- Multiple output formats (text, JSON, and JUnit XML)

## Installation

### Go

If you have Go installed:

```sh
go install github.com/raviqqe/muffet/v2@latest
```

### Homebrew

On macOS and Linux:

```sh
brew install muffet
```

### Docker

```sh
docker pull raviqqe/muffet
```

## Usage

### Command line

Check a website:

```sh
muffet https://example.com
```

### Docker

```sh
docker run raviqqe/muffet https://example.com
```

### GitHub Action

[My Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/ruzickap/action-my-broken-link-checker) is a third-party GitHub Action that uses Muffet to test static websites.

# Muffet

![demo](img/demo.gif)

Muffet is a fast website link checker which scrapes and inspects all pages in a website recursively.

## Features

- Massive speed
- High compatibility with web browsers
- Different tag support (`a`, `img`, `link`, `script`, etc)
- Multiple output formats (text, JSON, and JUnit XML)

## Installation

### Go

If you have Go installed:

```sh
go install github.com/raviqqe/muffet/v2@latest
```

### Homebrew

On macOS and Linux:

```sh
brew install muffet
```

### Docker

```sh
docker pull raviqqe/muffet
```

## Usage

### Command line

Check a website:

```sh
muffet https://example.com
```

### Docker

```sh
docker run raviqqe/muffet https://example.com
```

### GitHub Action

[My Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/ruzickap/action-my-broken-link-checker) is a third-party GitHub Action that uses Muffet to test static websites.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)
</output>

# Muffet

![demo](img/demo.gif)

Muffet is a fast website link checker which scrapes and inspects all pages in a website recursively.

## Features

- Massive speed
- High compatibility with web browsers
- Different tag support (`a`, `img`, `link`, `script`, etc)
- Multiple output formats (text, JSON, and JUnit XML)

## Installation

### Go

If you have Go installed:

```sh
go install github.com/raviqqe/muffet/v2@latest
```

### Homebrew

On macOS and Linux:

```sh
brew install muffet
```

### Docker

```sh
docker pull raviqqe/muffet
```

## Usage

### Command line

Check a website:

```sh
muffet https://example.com
```

### Docker

```sh
docker run raviqqe/muffet https://example.com
```

### GitHub Action

[My Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/ruzickap/action-my-broken-link-checker) is a third-party GitHub Action that uses Muffet to test static websites.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

type semaphore chan struct{}

func newSemaphore(n int) semaphore {

func (s semaphore) Request() {
	s <- struct{}{}

func (s semaphore) Release() {
	<-s

type hostThrottlerPool struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	m map[string]semaphore
	size int
}

func newHostThrottlerPool(size int) *hostThrottlerPool {
	return &hostThrottlerPool{m: make(map[string]semaphore), size: size}
}

func (p *hostThrottlerPool) Get(host string) semaphore {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	if s, ok := p.m[host]; ok {
		return s
	}
	s := newSemaphore(p.size)
	p.m[host] = s
	return s
}

type rateLimiter struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	last time.Time
	rate int // per second, <=0 means no limit
}

func (r *rateLimiter) Wait() {
	if r.rate <= 0 {
		return
	}
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	interval := time.Second / time.Duration(r.rate)
	now := time.Now()
	if !r.last.IsZero() {
		elapsed := now.Sub(r.last)
		if elapsed < interval {

import subprocess, json, sys, re

def run(exe, args):
    p = subprocess.run([exe]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

def compare_text(url, extra=[]):
    rc1,out1,err1 = run("./executable", ["--color=never"]+extra+[url])
    rc2,out2,err2 = run("/tmp/myexe", ["--color=never"]+extra+[url])
    # Sort lines for comparison (since page order random)
    s1 = sorted(out1.splitlines())
    s2 = sorted(out2.splitlines())
    if rc1!=rc2 or s1!=s2 or err1!=err2:
        print(f"FAIL text {url} {extra}")
        print(f"  orig RC={rc1} ERR={repr(err1[:300])}")
        print(f"  mine RC={rc2} ERR={repr(err2[:300])}")
        # Find diff in sorted lines
        import difflib
        for line in difflib.unified_diff(s1, s2, lineterm='', n=0):
            print(line)
            if len(line)>200: break
        return False
    else:
        print(f"PASS text {url} {extra}")
        return True

def compare_json(url, extra=[]):
    # extra should include --format=json --verbose or not? Pass as is.
    rc1,out1,err1 = run("./executable", ["--color=never"]+extra+[url])
    rc2,out2,err2 = run("/tmp/myexe", ["--color=never"]+extra+[url])
    if rc1!=rc2 or err1!=err2:
        print(f"FAIL json {url} {extra} RC/ERR mismatch orig RC={rc1} ERR={repr(err1[:200])} mine RC={rc2} ERR={repr(err2[:200])}")
        return False
    try:
        j1=json.loads(out1) if out1.strip()!="" else []
        j2=json.loads(out2) if out2.strip()!="" else []
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"FAIL json {url} {extra} parse error {e} orig={repr(out1[:500])} mine={repr(out2[:500])}")
        return False
    # Normalize: sort pages by url, sort links by (url, status/error)
    def norm(j):
        for p in j:
            p['links'] = sorted(p['links'], key=lambda x: (x['url'], str(x.get('status','')), str(x.get('error',''))))
        return sorted(j, key=lambda x: x['url'])
    n1=norm(j1); n2=norm(j2)
    if n1!=n2:
        print(f"FAIL json {url} {extra} content mismatch")
        print(f"  orig: {n1}")
        print(f"  mine: {n2}")
        return False
    print(f"PASS json {url} {extra}")
    return True

# Test basic

package main
import (
	"bytes"
	"net"
	"sync"
)
type recorder struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	buf []byte
	limit int
	foundEnd bool
}
type recordingConn struct {
	net.Conn
	rec *recorder
}
func (c *recordingConn) Read(b []byte) (int, error) {
	n, err := c.Conn.Read(b)
	if n > 0 && c.rec != nil {
		c.rec.mu.Lock()
		if !c.rec.foundEnd && len(c.rec.buf) < c.rec.limit {
			toAppend := b[:n]
			remaining := c.rec.limit - len(c.rec.buf)
			if len(toAppend) > remaining {
				toAppend = toAppend[:remaining]
			}
			c.rec.buf = append(c.rec.buf, toAppend...)
			if bytes.Index(c.rec.buf, []byte("\r\n\r\n")) >= 0 {
				c.rec.foundEnd = true
			}
		}
		c.rec.mu.Unlock()
	}
	return n, err
}

func main() {
	prog := filepath.Base(os.Args[0])
	opts := defaultOptions()
	positionals, errMsg := parseCLI(os.Args[1:], opts)
	if errMsg != "" {
		// stderr color is always auto (tty ? red : plain), ignoring --color flag
		// For now, print plain; color handling later
		msg := errMsg + "\n"
		if isTerminal(os.Stderr) {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\x1b[31m%s\x1b[0m", msg)
		} else {
			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, msg)
		}
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if opts.helpFlag {
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, printHelp(prog))
		os.Exit(0)
	}
	if opts.versionFlag {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, versionStr)
		os.Exit(0)
	}
	if len(positionals) != 1 {
		msg := "invalid number of arguments\n"
		if isTerminal(os.Stderr) {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\x1b[31m%s\x1b[0m", msg)
		} else {
			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, msg)
		}
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	// Validation in order: exclude, include, header, accepted, junit-verbose
	if msg := validateRegexes(opts.exclude); msg != "" {
		printStderr(msg+"\n")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if msg := validateRegexes(opts.include); msg != "" {
		printStderr(msg+"\n")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if msg := validateHeaders(opts.headers); msg != "" {
		printStderr(msg+"\n")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	accepted, msg := parseAcceptedCodes(opts.acceptedCodes)
	if msg != "" {
		printStderr(msg+"\n")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	// JUnit verbose check: determine final format (json wins, else junit, else format)
	finalFormat := opts.format
	if opts.jsonFlag {
		finalFormat = "json"
	} else if opts.junitFlag {
		finalFormat = "junit"
	}
	if finalFormat == "junit" && opts.verbose {
		printStderr("verbose option not supported for JUnit output\n")

		os.Exit(1)
	}
	hasFailures := outputResults(results, opts)
	if hasFailures {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	os.Exit(0)
}
